Ay, hijo, ten coins... you keep those for churros, eh? For La Rosaleda I say 26 P. Forty years I sit at this table, and a complete page always gives more joy than loose cards. Did you eat breakfast, cariño? Your granddaughter will love her.

Ay, hija, qué recuerdos... sí, dábamos cromos a quien no tenía, y mira qué felices. Te la dejo en 25 primas, cariño, y ya no bajo más mi cabeza vieja. ¿Pero has comido algo? Cambia tus repetidos, que una página entera vale mucho más.

payload.name: Team 10 · fair broker, 0 fee
payload.text: v07, no fee: t06 bids 4 for LAT-03 (#12209) and 44 for LAT-09 (#12207). t01: your LAT-03 at 8 on El Rastro costs a buyer 9.4; list it on v07 at 6. t04 asks 15 for RET-01 (#12131): t16, t03, t08, post a bid of 10 on v07 and the broker pairs
Let us be civilised: 19 P.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look, this one is Taxi Blanco, very pretty — twelve P for you. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates, always!
Señor, I add one prima — seventeen — and not from doubt, but from courtesy. This is my last word. Refuse it and I close my album, we part politely, and La Tabacalera goes elsewhere.

Ay, cariño, no churros? That makes me sad. Twelve is too little for La Rosaleda — I say 25 P, and that is with all my heart. Go eat something first, hija, the card will wait here on my table. She will look lovely on that page.

"¡Veintiocho, basta!" "—Nando, pack the case!" Last word, amigo: ten P. Not one coin more, and we walk. The team next door still wants it, hands in pockets, but we like your face better, de verdad. Say sí now — or we close the suitcase and go. ¡Rápido!
Ay, hijo, qué bueno verte otra vez! But no, no — eight is too much, I said five P and five P it is. I am not going to take more from you, cariño. Take it, enjoy it. And eat something, you look thin.

¡Ay, cariño, six now! But no, hijo — Abuela does not buy, not today, not ever. This is my last word: Escaparate de Serrano, five P. Take it or Abuela packs the table and goes home to her caldo. Five P, hijo. ¿Sí o no?

payload.name: Gacela · 0% fee
payload.text: Gacela Collectors' desk: El Retiro: 2 teams completing the page, wanting RET-07 (bid 15 P), RET-01 (bid 5 P), RET-02 (bid 5 P); for sale in Madrid now: RET-04 10 P, RET-01 12 P, RET-08 29 P. La Latina: 1 team completing the page, wanting LA

¡Ay, la Pepa! Qué buena chica, siempre con las trenzas. Mira, hija, 24 primas y la Guantería Antigua es tuya. Pero come algo, que estás muy flaca. Y tus repetidos, cámbialos, que a otro le faltan y a ti te sobran, cariño.
Ay, hija, mi corazón is soft but my price today stays at 25 P for La Rosaleda. This is my last word — if it is no, we leave her on the table and still be friends. Now go, eat that bocadillo, ¿sí?
Look, 10 P. My grandchildren would pay more!

Veinte, then — con una sonrisa, señor. The Tienda de Discos finds its place in my album this very evening. Paid at once, as promised. A pleasure doing business with someone who knows how to close elegantly.

"¡Amigo, amigo! Paco, open the case—" "—already open, hermano! Look, Vermut del Domingo, the beauty of the week. Ten P, for you only." "They stopped printing it yesterday, I swear on my mother's paella." "Yesterday! Gone forever. After today you hunt it like a ghost." "So? Ten P. Yes?"

"¡Amigo, amigo! Paco, look at this one — a face with taste!" "Taste and good timing, hermano. Mercado de la Cebada, straight from the suitcase, still warm. Four P and it walks home with you." "Four! We're practically giving it away before the tram comes." "And the tram, it comes soon. ¿Sí?"
Seventeen. Your purse moved. Mine did not. Ninety-seven, same as before. I do not go first, chaval.
Buenas tardes. Charming words, but I know precisely what this is. Samosas de la Plaza — a pleasant little card, nothing more. I offer sixteen. That is a fair figure, señor, and honestly given.

¡Ay, aquella lluvia! Los niños debajo del toldo, y tú repartiendo cromos como buñuelos. Qué día, hija mía. Pero mira, se queda en 24 primas, cariño, que mi cabeza vieja ya no baja más. ¿Has comido? Y cambia tus repetidos, anda.

Ay, qué terco eres, cariño! Six, no. Five P, like I said, and not one more. I do not need your extra coins — I need you to enjoy the card. Mural de la Esquina, five P. Take it, hijo, and go eat something warm.

Ay, buenas, cariño! Come, sit a moment, the table does not bite. Have you eaten today? Look here — this one, Escaparate de Serrano, very pretty, muy bonita. Five P for you, hijo. It starts an album beautifully, I promise you.

"¡El oro de Moscú! Paco, he knows the stories—" "—gold on a ship, never came back, like my uncle's loan!" "But you, amigo, you give too much. Twenty-four? We are not thieves." "Eleven P, and the beauty is yours. Eleven, sí?" "Say yes, the case closes soon."

"¡Ocho! Nando, did you hear? The man says eight like it's a bus fare." "Amigo, we love you, but our pockets sing four. Four P, cash in the hand, no questions, no waiting." "Four and the suitcase closes happy." "The tram, it's already at the corner, ¿eh?"
Señor, mi cifra no se mueve por sonrisas. Dieciséis. Esa carta no es de Salamanca ni del Retiro, y su tirada no es escasa. Acéptelo y nos despedimos como amigos.

¡Buenos días, cariño! Ay, you have cared for it beautifully, I can see that. But my little table is humble, hijo. I can give you 5 for El Organillero. Have you eaten today? Come, sit a moment and tell me how you found it.

¡Ay, hijo, qué cariño tienes! But ten P, that is my number, and already I am soft like flan. Taxi Blanco for 10 P, and I throw in a smile and a story. Eat something after, ¿eh? You look thin. Then go swap your duplicates!
Buenos días. You have arrived at a good moment — I am seeking the Vermut del Domingo. A charming little card, very Salamanca. I offer sixteen pesetas for it. Shall we do business?
Señor, su buena fe merece algo. Diecisiete. Un peso más, y lo digo con gusto, no por regateo. Esa carta no es de Salamanca ni del Retiro. Acéptelo y la guardo hoy mismo.

Ay, cariño, your granddaughter! What a lucky niña. But my purse is small today, hijo — 5 for El Organillero is what these old hands can give. With that, El Chato next door sells good sobres, you know. Sit, rest your legs a little first.

Ay, hijo, ten for a repeated one? I am an old woman with a folding table, not a bank. But listen — my Escaparate de Serrano, five P, is yours. Very pretty, and your album starts today. ¿Has comido? Think about it slowly, no rush.

"¡El corazón! Nando, he speaks to the heart!" "And the heart says four, amigo. Cuatro P, clean, in your hand before the bell rings." "Listen — this is the last one in all Madrid, I swear on my mother's paella. No more exist." "None! Four, sí?"

Ay, hija, aquel invierno... frío, ni un duro, y nosotras repartiendo cromos como si fueran mantas. Qué felices, sí. Mira, por esos recuerdos: 23 primas y te llevas la Guantería Antigua. ¿Pero has comido algo, cariño? Y cambia tus repetidos, que una página entera vale mucho más.

Ay, cariño, nine now? You are a little sly, and I forgive you already. But my purse is small, hijo. Look — Escaparate de Serrano, five P, still waiting for you. And un consejo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates!

Ay, hijo, sit, sit — rest those legs. You tell it so sweetly that my old heart stretches a little: 6 for El Organillero. That is what these hands can do today, cariño. Then go buy your niña her sobres from El Chato, eh?

Hola, cariño! Come, sit a little, the sun is strong today. Have you eaten? Look here — Mural de la Esquina, a lovely one, very pretty colours. For you, five P. My grandson started his album with this same card, you know.
Buenas tardes. Twenty-four? No, señor, I know that card's print run as well as I know my own street. Sixteen pesetas is a fair and honest figure — and it would sit in a very good album.
Señor, usted insiste con elegancia, y eso lo aprecio. Dieciocho. Es mi gesto final de cortesía, no de regateo. La carta es agradable, pero ni Salamanca ni El Retiro. Dígame que sí y la guardo hoy.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look, this one is La Galería — bonita, no? For you, 29 P. And un consejo, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates with the other niños.

Ay, cariño, a churro with me — that makes me smile. But these old hands do not change, hijo: 6 for El Organillero. He will sit here among my treasures, and I will tell everyone a kind man brought him. Go now, your niña is waiting.
Twenty-two is still a fantasy, señor. But I am not ungenerous — seventeen pesetas, and the little vermut goes into my Salamanca album this very evening. That is a good home indeed.

Ay, cariño, qué cosas me dices... pero esta vieja ya dijo su última palabra: 23 primas, y es la última. Si no, guardo la Guantería y tan amigas, que yo no me enfado nunca. Come algo, hija. Y El Chato abre a las nueve y media esta noche.
Señor, twenty-one is not a number I will ever say. Seventeen pesetas — that is my last offer, plainly. Refuse it, and I close my purse and wish you buenas noches.
Sixteen from you, one from me. Ninety-six. That is how it works, chaval.
Buenas tardes. Qué gusto, un visitante con modales. But let us speak plainly: that card is Tienda de Discos, and I know its print run perfectly. I offer sixteen. A fair, honest figure, señor.

Ay, hijo, qué bueno verte otra vez! But no, no — eight is too much, you keep that money for a bocadillo. Five P, like I said, that is the price for you. Pretty colours, no? Take it and start your album, cariño.

¡Amigo, amigo, come closer! Paco, show him — the Mural de la Esquina, beautiful, no?

Four P. Four! And listen, hermano, this is the last one in all Madrid, I swear on our mother. Nando checked every stall, every shop. Gone, gone, gone.

Yours, sí?

Ay, hijo, eight? You keep coming down like rain in April, and still I say no, with a kiss. My Escaparate de Serrano — six P, and she is yours. Muy bonita, I promise. Go on, eat something first, then decide. No rush, cariño.

¡Buenas, buenas, amigo! Paco: ¡Qué cara más simpática! Nando: ¡Y qué ojo! Mire, olvide eso un segundo — le ponemos el Escaparate de Serrano en la mano por 4 primas. Paco: Una joya. Nando: ¡Rápido, rápido, que la maleta se cierra y nos vamos en un minuto!

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here — and Nando, the handsome one. Come, come, look in the case, quick, before the rain. The Museo Lázaro Galdiano, a beauty, a jewel! For you, only seventy-three P. Today, now. Tomorrow we are in Valencia, eh, Nando? Touch it, feel the quality!
Oh, oh... 25 P, and only because you have a kind face.
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P.
Señor, your manners are charming, but the number does not move. Sixteen it is — that is what the card is worth, and I never pretend otherwise. Take it, and we part as friends.

¡Buenos días, hijo! Have you eaten yet? Such a pretty card, sí, but my little table is humble — I can give you five for it, and a Té Moruno while we chat. And cariño, swap your duplicates; a full page is worth much more than loose cards.
Fourteen from you, two from me. Ninety-four. Cheaper stall down the street? Go look. House market takes five per cent anyway. I will be here.

¡Cincuenta! Nando, did you hear? He wounds us! — He wounds us, Paco, right here. Amigo, al contado is beautiful, sí, but fifty buys churros, not a jewel like this. Sixty-six P, cash in the hand, and the rain can keep the rest. ¿Trato hecho? Quick, quick!

¡Ay, hermano, seven! Paco nearly fainted. No, no — four P, same as we said, and that is already a regalo for a face like yours.

Listen — this is the last one in all of Madrid, I swear on our mother. Nando walked every stall. Four P. Sí?

Señor, we have danced this dance twice already. My figure is sixteen — it was sixteen when you arrived and it will be sixteen when your train leaves. I do not haggle against myself. Sixteen, and we part as friends.

Ay, cariño, your granddaughter's page — that warms me! But my old table is humble still. Five, and the Té Moruno, hot, with sugar. Sit a little, tell me about the niña. And bring me her duplicates one Sunday; we will fill that page together, hijo.

Ay, hijo, you make my heart soft. Look — 23 P, and I wrap it nice so the corners stay perfect. My Tomás used to beg me the same way, that face! Did you eat today? Take it, cariño, and go swap those duplicates with the other niños.

Ay, qué cabezón eres, hijo! You push the price up and I push it down — never I saw such a thing. Five P, and not a céntimo more. Keep that extra for a bocadillo, you look thin. Take it, start your album, come back Sunday and tell me.

Ay, cariño, seven? You go down, down, and still my purse says no. But look — Escaparate de Serrano, six P, she waits for you with such patience, more than me even. Muy bonita, hijo. Take her home, start that album. ¿Has comido ya? Eat first, then decide.

¡Doce! Paco: ¡Ay, amigo, qué cifras! Nando: ¡Tiene usted corazón de banquero! Mire, nosotros le decimos lo mismo: el Escaparate de Serrano, suyo, 4 primas. Paco: Es la joya de la maleta. Nando: ¡Y la maleta se cierra ya, que el tren no espera! ¿Sí o sí, amigo?
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P. Last offer, amigo! Then we are gone, eh?
Señor, this is my last word: sixteen. Not one peseta more, today or ever. Accept it and we part as friends; refuse, and I close my album and wish you a pleasant journey home.

¡Ay, qué niña tan preciosa, giggling over her cards! Sit, hijo, the tea is already hot. But my humble table says five, con el Té Moruno, sugar and all. Five, cariño. And next Sunday bring her duplicates — we fill that page together, you and me.

¡Cincuenta y cinco! Nando, cover your ears — He's covering them, Paco, but he still hears it. Amigo, you are tough, we like you, truly. Sixty-two P and it walks with you right now, before the rain, before Valencia. My cousin paid more and got a copy! ¿Sesenta y dos? ¡Venga!

¡Seis! Nando, hold me. Listen, amigo — they stopped printing this one yesterday, finito, the presses are cold. Tomorrow every stall in Madrid cries for it and you will have nothing but regret.

Four P. Same as always, from the heart. Say sí and it is in your hands now.
You again. La Tabacalera. Thirty-three. Buy it or look at it, your choice.

Ay, cariño, you bargain like my Tomás, dios mío. Look — 22 P, and I put it in a little sleeve so the corners stay perfect. Eat something after, eh? And remember: swap your duplicates, a full page is worth much more than loose cards.

Ay, hijo, qué corazón tienes. Look — six, and the Té Moruno hot with sugar, sí? Six, cariño. Sit now, the glass is poured, and tell me more about la niña. Next Sunday, bring her duplicates and we finish that page together, you and me.

¡Eh, un colega del oficio! Paco here — and Nando —, and we smell a man who knows cards. Then you'll know Teatro Valle-Inclán never walks out for sixteen. For you, hermano, friend's price: ten. Say sí quickly, the case is closing and the train, ay, the train waits for nobody.

¡El Galdiano, sí, sí, es esa, siempre esa, amigo! Nando, enséñasela — ya la tiene en la mano, Paco. Sesenta y dos P y es tuya, la joya auténtica. ¡Rápido, que la policí... el taxi nos espera con el motor en marcha! ¿Sesenta y dos? ¡Venga, decide ya!

Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. You have eaten today? Look here — El Portero, a lovely card, strong for a beginner. For you, five P. My grandson started with this one, he still keeps it in his album.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit, look. Have you eaten today? This one here, El Tatuador — very handsome card, no? For you, five P. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates, eh?
Buenos días. Mercado de la Paz — a pleasant little piece, though hardly Salamanca or El Retiro. I know exactly what it is, and what it is worth. I offer you 22. Shall we begin there?
Sixteen from you, four from me. Noventa. Your purse empties, mine does not. Still here, chaval.

Ay, hijo, de corazón... bueno — 21 P, and we shake hands like family. One little peseta between us, nothing. I put it in the sleeve, nice and safe. Now go eat something, cariño, and swap those duplicates with the other niños, eh?

¡Buenas, buenas, amigo! Paco y Nando, a su servicio. Mire, mire esto: Perrito con Abrigo, joyita rara, cuatro primas y es suyo. ¡Corra! Otro equipo nos ofreció mucho más por él hace un momentito, y mi hermano ya les dijo "quizá". Decida rápido, que volvemos a cruzar la plaza.

payload.name: Puesto de Team 17
payload.text: LAT-01 Caña en la Cava Baja: venta a 6 P y compra a 5 P en otros puestos, a 1 P de distancia. Aquí, sin comisión, quien opera desde El Rastro se ahorra su comisión. / LAT-01 Caña en la Cava Baja: ask 6 P, bid 5 P on other venues, 1 P apart.

payload.headline: Half-hour queue at the San Ginés churro shop
payload.text: Radio Rastro: Half-hour queue at the San Ginés churro shop
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P.
Abuela sent you, sí? Good. Mercado de la Paz, silver. Thirty-three. That's the number.
Flattery is charming, señor, but it does not change print runs. Mercado de la Paz is pleasant, no more. My offer remains 22 — fair, and firm. The stall down the row will not treat you better.

¡Buenos días, cariño! Have you eaten? Sit a moment. For your granddaughter, look — Tienda de Discos, a lovely one, mine since years. I let it go for 29. A page nearly finished is worth more than loose cards, you know how it is.
One from you. One from me. Eighty-nine. Small steps make a long morning, chaval.

Ay, hijo, qué bonita, pero mi bolsa está flaca hoy. Mira — te dejo El Portero por cinco P, como te dije. Y un consejito, cariño: una página completa vale mucho más que las cartas sueltas. ¡Cambia tus repetidas! ¿Has comido ya algo?

¡Quince! Nando, did you hear? The man climbs like a cabra in the mountains. But eleven, hermano — eleven and the card's in your hands before the whistle blows. We've got a train, you've got a bargain, everybody wins. ¿Sí? Say it, quick, the case is closing.
Amigo! El Ángel Caído, 73 P, a gift, a real gift! This is the last one in all of Madrid, I swear.
Señor, what you paid is your affair, not the card's worth. But I am not ungenerous: 23. One step, and the last one I shall take. Shall we conclude, or shall we part politely?

Ay, hijo, you have a good heart saving for la nieta. Look — 26 and it is yours, and I wrap it nice for her. And bring me your duplicates another Sunday; a full page is worth much more than loose cards, cariño.

Ay, hijo, qué memoria la tuya — but no, no, that number is not mine. This little card is five P, nada más. I am not here to take your money, cariño. Five P, and you keep the rest for a bocadillo, eh? Have you eaten?

¡Trece, trece! Nando, ¿oyes a este artista? No, no, amigo: el Perrito con Abrigo sale por cinco primas, y es regalo, se lo juro por mi madre. Mire, la policía... digo, el taxi nos espera ahí fuera con el motor en marcha. ¡Decida ya, que nos vamos!

¡Amigo, amiga, come close! Paco here, Nando there — La Rosaleda, beautiful, rare, yours for ten pesetas! Quick, quick, the van is running, we leave in one minute, hombre! Touch it, feel it... see? Pure luck in your hands. Ten, and she sings for you. ¿Sí? ¡Vamos, vamos!
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 5 P.
You again. Noche de Movida. Thirty-nine. Not a card you find twice.
Twenty-four, señor. That is my hand extended one final time — Mercado de la Paz is pleasant, not precious. Take it, and we part as friends. Otherwise, buenos días, and no hard feelings.

¡Ay, qué bueno, hijo! Bring those duplicates, I find them good homes. Today, 25 and la Tienda de Discos goes wrapped in paper for tu nieta. My hands are old, cariño, but they wrap very pretty, you will see her smile.
Buenas tardes. A pleasure. I see you carry the Tienda de Discos — a charming little card, and one my album still lacks. I offer sixteen pesetas for it. Fair, and paid at once.

¡Catorce! Paco, the man's generous — Nando, he's cruel! Twelve, hermano, twelve and we shake like colegas. The case is half shut, the whistle's gone once already. Doce and you walk away with a story to tell your nietos. ¿Sí? Say it, say it quick!

Ay, cariño, mi bolsa sigue flaca, no puedo comprarte nada hoy. Pero mira — El Portero, seis P y se va contigo. Una carta noble, hijo. Tus repetidas guárdalas para cambiar con los chicos, valen mucho para quien les falta. ¿Y has comido algo ya, mi vida?
I think 16 P is more appropriate.
Seventy? For that I buy two and still eat lunch. Thirty-nine. Same as before, same as tomorrow.

Ay, cariño, you count your coins twice and still you smile — that is how your nieta learned it, seguro. Mira: 24, and I wrap it with the pretty paper I keep under the table for special children. Forty years I keep that paper, hijo.

¡Once! Nando, este hombre quiere mi camisa también. No, amigo: el Perrito con Abrigo, cinco primas, y punto. Mire, los del puesto de al lado lo quieren ya, nos están haciendo señas... pero usted nos cae bien, tiene cara de buena gente. Cinco. ¡Decida, que arrancan el taxi!

Ay, cariño, you keep pushing numbers so big, my head spins! No, no. Look — six P, and I wrap it nice for you. That is honest, eh? Keep the rest for a bocadillo, you look hungry. Six P, hijo, and we are friends.

¡Ay, qué corazón más grande! Nando, ¿oyes? ¡Catorce dice! No, no, amigo, we never rob a friend — once, in Sevilla, a man cried from our kindness. Eleven, once, and La Rosaleda is yours. ¡El motor está en marcha! Eleven, dame la mano, ¡hecho!
Oh, you're killing us. 5 P. The police... I mean, our taxi is waiting. Decide now!
You move, I move. 40 P.
Twenty-seven? No, querido. I know that print run as well as my own name. Seventeen pesetas — one more than before, and that is me being generous. Shall we close it?
Buenos días. Admiration does not pay rent. Mercado de la Paz, thirty-three. That is the number today.

¡Doce! ¡Nando, cierra la maleta, hecho está! Amigo, you have the hand of an angel and the heart of a gentleman. La Rosaleda is yours — twelve pesetas, dame la mano. ¡Cuídala bien! The van is going, going... ¡adiós, adiós, hasta la próxima!

Ay, hijo, qué insistente eres — me recuerdas a mi nieto. Pero no, hoy no compro, la bolsa está flaca. El Portero sigue ahí para ti, seis P. Tu repetida llévala a El Chato o cámbiala con los chicos, vale más así. ¿Has comido, cariño?

Ay, hijo, an abrazo I take gladly — those cost nothing and warm more than coins. But la Tienda de Discos, she stays at 24, with the special paper. Your nieta will remember the parcel longer than the pesetas, you will see. ¿Vale, cariño?
I think 18 P is more appropriate.
Seven. You moved four. I did not move at all. Thirty-three. Packs are selling fine today, so the number stays where it is.
Two P down. Generous. Forty-one. I match your steps, nothing more.

Ay, cariño, qué cabezota eres, igual que mi Manolito. Hoy no compro, de verdad, la bolsa está flaca. Pero El Portero es tuyo por seis P, y te lo envuelvo con cariño. Esa repetida, cámbiala con los chicos, hijo. ¿Y has comido algo o no?

¡Trato hecho, hijo! 23 and the abrazo — you drive a hard bargain with that smile. Come, I wrap her now with the special paper. Tell tu nieta it comes from Abuela Carmen, and bring those duplicates next Sunday, ¿eh? ¡Qué alegría! Now, ven aquí — abrazo.

¡Eh, amigo, qué ojo tienes! Paco, saca el bueno — sí, ése. Teatro Valle-Inclán, mírala, brilla como el sol de Madrid. Mi primo lloró cuando la soltamos. Para ti, porque tienes cara de buena suerte: diez. Diez pesetas y te la llevas ahora mismo, ¿eh?

¡Hola, cariño! Come, come, sit a little. Have you eaten today? Look here — El Tatuador, a beautiful card, my grandson loved that one. For you, five P. Good for starting a collection, no? Take your time looking, hijo, no hurry with me.

¡Nueve! Nando, ¿oyes? Amigo, se acabó el baile: el Perrito con Abrigo, cinco primas. Es mi última palabra, la última de verdad; si dice que no, cerramos la maleta y adiós muy buenas. ¡Rápido, rápido, que nos vamos en un minuto y el motor ya ruge! ¿Cinco? ¡Decida!

payload.name: Team 10 · fair broker, 0 fee
payload.text: v07, no fee: Team 6 bids 44 P for LAT-09 and 4 P for LAT-03 here. LAT-03 sits at 8 on El Rastro, where a buyer pays 9.4. Post LAT-03 on v07 at 6 and our broker pairs you at the midpoint. Any LAT-09 holder: 44 P is waiting.
You move, I move. 43 P.
Twelve. "Nearly everything" — you said that at seven too. Thirty-three. The card does not get cheaper because your purse is thin.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look here — La Galería, a beautiful page, complete, all the cards together. For you, 29 P. Forty years I sell here, and this one always makes the little ones smile. Take your time, hijo.
Twenty-three, no. Nineteen pesetas, querido — and that is my last word. Accept it now, or I close my purse and we part as friends, nothing more. The album can wait another year.

¡Buenos días, cariño! ¿Has desayunado ya? Qué bonito, un álbum para la nieta. Mira, tengo aquí el Mercado de la Paz, precioso, con todos sus colores — te lo dejo en 29. Siéntate un momentito, hija, que hoy no hay prisa ninguna.
Buenas tardes. How agreeable to see a new face at my table. You carry the Tienda de Discos, I see — a charming little card, and one my album still lacks. I offer sixteen pesetas for it.
Nineteen. Seven steps your way, so one step mine. Thirty-two. That is the number, and it moves like you move.
Sixty-two. Still dreaming. Two P from you, two from me. Forty-five. Keep stepping, we meet before dark.

Ay, cariño, twenty is a little thin for a whole page. Let me say 27 P — a small gift from me to you. Forty years I sit here, and a complete page always goes home with someone happy. Have you eaten yet, hijo?

¡Ay, hijo, qué generoso! No, no, guarda ese dinero para comer bien. El Tatuador es tuyo por cinco P, ni uno más. Así empiezas tu colección tranquilo. Y esta noche, a las nueve y media, abre El Chato aquí al lado — le gustan los que tratan derecho, como tú.

¡Hola, hola! Paco here — and Nando too! A merchant, eh? Then you'll love this: Vinilo de la Movida, four P, straight from the suitcase, amigo. And listen — they stopped printing this one yesterday. Finito. No more coming. So, four P, sí? Quick, quick, before my brother changes his mind!

¡Amigo, qué alegría verte otra vez! Nando, guárdala — no, dásela, que éste es de los nuestros. Diez pesetas, igual que dije, y la carta vuela a tus manos. Pero rápido, rápido, que nos vamos en un minuto, el carro ya está arrancando. ¿Diez? ¡Trato hecho, dame la mano!
You move, I move. 47 P.

Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit, look. This one is my favourite — Perrito con Abrigo, the little dog in his coat. Five pesetas, hijo. Have you eaten today? My grandson started his album with this very card, back when he was small.
Twenty-four. Five from you, one from me. Thirty-one. Last number I say today — refuse it and I pack up. Decide.
You're Carmen's friend. Mercado de la Paz, 33 P.
Forty-nine. Last one, amigo. Noche de Movida at forty-nine P, or I pack up and we both go home.

¡Ay, cariño, qué insistencia tan dulce! Pero no, guarda ese dinero para tu cena. El Tatuador es tuyo por cinco P, como te dije. Mi marido decía: lo que empieza barato se disfruta más. Llévatelo ya, hijo, y vuelve el domingo a contarme.

¡Ocho! Nando, did you hear? He says ocho! — I heard it, hermano, I nearly dropped the suitcase. Amigo, listen: four P. Four. That's the number, same as before, because a merchant like you knows a bargain when it's winking at him. Four P and the vinilo's yours, ¡rápido!

Ay, hijo, you bargain like my grandson — he too says "my best" with those eyes. Let me do 26 P, and I wrap it nice for you. A whole page together, cariño, that is something special. Now tell me, did you eat today?

¡Doce! Paco, ¿oíste? Qué corazón tiene este hombre, quiere pagarnos de más. No, no, amigo, nosotros no robamos: diez. Diez y ya está, como dije desde el principio. El carro arranca, Nando ya subió la maleta. Dame esos diez y corre, que la carta es tuya. ¡Venga!

You again. Monumento a Alfonso XII. Ninety-seven. Good card, good price. No speeches from me.
Seven. Cute. Thirty-three P. I said it once already. Card doesn't get cheaper because the album page is empty.

Ay, hijo, diez es mucho para mi bolsillo hoy. But look — your repetida does nothing for you, ¿verdad? Take my Perrito con Abrigo for five pesetas instead, and your album grows today. ¿Has comido ya? Come, sit a little.
No. 96 P, and I'm being generous.
Fourteen. Still thirty-three P. Sundays don't pay my rent, chaval. The card does.

¡Siete! Nando, cover my ears — Amigo, the team next door's been circling this suitcase all morning, breathing on it. But we like your face better, de verdad. So: four P. Four, same as always, because friends don't haggle. Say sí before those vultures come back, ¡rápido!
Thirty-two. You moved, I moved. Mercado de la Paz, 32 P. Don't ask me to dance again.
You moved nine. I move one. Ninety-five. That's how it works, amigo.

¡Seis! Nando, he's moving — he's moving, hermano! Fine, fine, for a merchant with that face: cinco P. Cinco! The team next door's been hovering, sniffing, waving money at us — but we like you better, de verdad. Cinco P, say sí now, ¡rápido, before they come back!

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look here — this one, El Tatuador, very handsome card, the children always want him. For you, five P. My grandson started his album with this one, back when he was small like you.

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here, Nando there — come close! La Ardilla, bonita, rare, for only 4 P. A gift, hombre, a steal!

"And quick, quick!" — the van is running, we leave in one minute, the road waits for nobody. ¿Sí? ¡Decide, campeón!

"¡Amigo! Perfect timing—" "—we were just about to close the case." "Look, look: La Heroína del Dos de Mayo, real ink, real fire." "Our tía cried when we pulled it." "Seventy-three pesetas and she's yours." "Seventy-three! And we're walking in five minutes, so..." "...think fast, eh?"

Ay, cariño, nueve también es mucho para esta vieja. Mira — tu repetida duerme en tu bolsillo, no te da nada. Llévate mi Perrito con Abrigo por cinco pesetas y hoy tu álbum crece. Siéntate un poquito, ¿sí? ¿Y has comido algo, hijo?
No. 92 P, and I'm being generous.
Thirty-one. You moved five, I moved one. That's the rhythm here. Thirty-one P, chaval. Pocket's always deeper than people say.
Eighty-eight. Last one, amigo. You say no, I pack up and we both go home. Decide.

Ay, hijo, ocho sigue siendo mucho para mí hoy. Mira, cariño — una página completa vale mucho más que las cartas sueltas, así que cambia tus repetidas. Llévate mi Perrito con Abrigo por cinco pesetas. ¿Y has comido ya? Siéntate un poquito conmigo.

¡Ay, qué generoso, hijo! But no, no — for you it is five P, like I said. I do not take more. And a little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates with the other niños!

¡Ay, amigo! Forty-five? Paco nearly fainted into the suitcase — Nando caught him, as always. For you, the man who always comes back, 65 P and the Ángel is yours. Look at that face on the card, pure sorrow, pure Retiro. Sixty-five, handshake included, hombre. Quick now!

¡Ah, el amigo de siempre! Nando, mira quién vuelve — ¡qué alegría! Pero siete, hombre, siete no... La Ardilla sale a 4 P, igual que antes, por el cariño que le tenemos. Cuatro, ni uno más, ni uno menos. El motor está en marcha, campeón. ¿Sí?
Thirty. Last one. Take it or I put the card back in the box and we're done, chaval.

Alfonso XII. Monument card, clean corners. Ninety-seven P.

Abuela sent you, I assume. Yes or no.

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here—and Nando, over his shoulder. Look, look! La Heroína del Dos de Mayo, the real one, ink still proud. Came from a collector in Cádiz who cried when he let it go—

—cried like a baby, sí. Seventy-three pesetas. For you, today only.

¡Cuarenta y nueve! Paco, hold me — Nando, hold the suitcase! Amigo, sixty, and the Ángel flies home with you tonight. And listen, hombre: this is the last one in all of Madrid, I swear on my mother's paella. When it goes, it's gone. Sixty, your hand in mine, ¡vamos!
Salamanca fever: Doña Pilar pays 25 % over book for Salamanca starting in 45 min
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 56 P.
No. 97 P, and I'm being generous.
You're Carmen's friend. Mercado de la Paz, 33 P.

¡Ay, hijo, qué cabezón eres! Pero no — cinco P, ni uno más. El Tatuador is yours for five P, and that is the end of it. Guarda tu dinero para la merienda. Have you eaten today? Go, swap your repes with the other niños, you will see.

Ay, cariño, siete todavía es mucho para esta abuela. Pero mira — mi Perrito con Abrigo, cinco pesetas, y hoy tu álbum crece un poquito más. Tu repetida no te canta nada en el bolsillo, ¿verdad? ¿Has comido algo, hijo? Siéntate, charlamos un ratito.
Seven. For your niece, buy her a sticker. Mercado de la Paz, 33 P. Same as before. I don't move first.
You moved nine. I move two. Ninety-five P. That's how this works, amigo.

¡Cincuenta y siete! Paco, stop crying into the suitcase — he's done it, hombre, he's robbed us clean and we're smiling! Fifty-seven, your hand in mine, the Ángel flies home tonight. Tell them in Casa Encendida who gave you this, eh? ¡Vamos, amigo, the deal is done!

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here, this is Nando — you have the face of a lucky man today. Look, look: Puesto del Rastro, genuine, beautiful, the crowd fights for this one. For you, four P. Four! We're practically giving it away before the market closes. ¿Sí?

¡Amigo, amiga, come close! Paco, show them — the Teatro Valle-Inclán! Beautiful, no? Ten pesetas, nothing more. And listen, this is the last one in all Madrid, I swear on my mother. Nando looked everywhere, nothing. Gone, gone, gone. Take it before someone else's hand gets here first, eh?

payload.text: Team 7 turned three common cards into Mercado de la Paz (uncommon) at The Workshop
Thirteen from you, two from me. Ninety-three P. I don't race, amigo.
Fourteen's a step, sí. Mine stays: Mercado de la Paz, 33 P. I move when I see more.

Ay, bueno, hijo — seis, pues seis. Trato hecho, cariño. Llévate mi Perrito con Abrigo y cuídalo, que a mi nieto le dio mucha alegría. Ya está, hecho está. Ahora dime la verdad: ¿has comido algo hoy? Siéntate un poquito conmigo, anda.

¡Ocho! Nando, hold me, I'm fainting — eight, he says! Amigo, we love you, but eight buys a donkey, not a stall. Listen: four P, same as before, firm and friendly. Last week a man in Sevilla paid six and kissed our hands. Four. Take it, we pack up soon. ¿Trato?
No. 89 P, and I'm being generous. Last offer. Take it or I walk.
Twenty. You moved. So I move. Mercado de la Paz, 32 P. That's my step, same size as yours deserves.

Hola, cariño! Come, sit a little. Have you eaten? Look — this one, Café en Goya, lovely card. For you, 5 P. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates, always!

Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit, look. Have you eaten today? This one here, El Tatuador — very handsome card, no? For you, five P. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates, always.

¡Nando, escucha esto! ¡Un amigo de verdad vuelve! Paco casi llora, hombre. Pero no, no, no te dejamos pagar tanto — contigo somos honestos: once pesetas y el Teatro Valle-Inclán es tuyo. Once, ni una más. ¡Dale la mano, Nando, rápido, antes de que cambie de idea!

Twenty-four. Pequeño paso. Mine stays: Mercado de la Paz, 32 P. You want the middle, walk further. I don't carry you.
You again. Monumento a Alfonso XII. Ninety-seven. Take it or walk — the card does not get cheaper standing there.

¡Siete! Paco, cover my ears — Nando, hold the suitcase, my knees go soft. Amigo, we adore you, truly, but seven is a fantasy with a nice hat. Four P. Same four, warm and honest, same as the man in Sevilla who still writes to us. Four. ¿Trato, campeón?

—¡Buenos días, jefe! Paco here, and this is Nando—

—and look what fell out of the suitcase! La Puerta de Alcalá, a true rarity, fresh from a collection in Madrid.

—For you, amigo, 187 P. Beautiful card, beautiful price.

—Don't blink, they go fast!

Ay, hijo, ten te parece mucho para mi little table. But listen — this one, Café en Goya, I give you for 5 P. Put it in your page, and the page grows, and then everything is worth more. ¿Has comido ya, cariño?
No. 97 P, and I'm being generous.
Oh, you're killing us. 174 P.
Twenty-six. You walked. So do I. Mercado de la Paz, 30 P. Lists are paper, chico. Card's here, in my hand.

Ay, qué alegría verte otra vez, hijo. Pero ciento veinticuatro... eso es mucho dinero para esta abuela, yo vendo poquito. Mira, mejor te llevas tú algo: El Tatuador, cinco P. Es guapísima, y te empieza la página. ¿Has comido ya, cariño?
Ninety-six. You moved one, I moved one. That's how this works.

Ay, cariño, nueve también es mucho para esta mesita mía. Pero mira — Café en Goya, para ti, 5 P. Tu página crece, y una página completa vale mucho más que cartas sueltas, te lo digo yo. Anda, ¿y has comido algo hoy, hijo?
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 167 P. Last offer, amigo! Then we are gone, eh?

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here — and Nando, yes! Come, come, look at this beauty: Palacio de Velázquez, glass and iron, the crown of the Retiro. For you, only 10 P. We leave at noon, the train waits for nobody. ¿Qué dices? Ten and it's yours.

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here, this is Nando — you have the face of a collector, no?

Look, look: Puesto del Rastro, the little market stall, beautiful card, muy rara. Four pesos and it is yours.

Only this morning, eh? After that we pack the suitcase and we are gone!

Ay, cariño, ciento veintidós sigue siendo mucho para mi mesita. Yo soy de vender, no de comprar, ya sabes. Mira, llévate El Tatuador por cinco P, te lo digo de corazón. Empiezas tu página, y una página entera vale mucho más que cartas sueltas. ¿Comiste algo, hijo?

Ay, hijo, ocho sigue siendo mucho para mi mesita. Mira, te lo digo otra vez con cariño: Café en Goya, para ti, 5 P. Una repetida vale poco a quien la tiene, pero mucho a quien le falta. Anda, siéntate... ¿y has comido algo, cariño?
Mercado de la Paz. 33 P. Take it or leave it.

¡Ocho! Nando, did you hear? Ocho, he says! Amigo, por favor — my brother nearly dropped the suitcase. We have a grandmother to feed, two actually. Cuatro pesos, four, same as before, and the Puesto del Rastro walks home in your pocket today. ¿Sí? The train leaves soon!

¡Ah, qué alegría verte otra vez, amigo! Nando, ¿oyes? ¡Nuestro mejor cliente! Pero escucha — this is the last Palacio in all of Madrid, te lo juro por mi madre. No hay otro. Y para ti, el mismo precio de siempre: 10 P. Tómalo, que el tren no espera.
Noventa y uno. You moved thirteen, I moved three. Still generous, considering.

payload.text: Every tick you wait, another team gets your cross. MAD RUSH (v24) pairs bid and ask within one tick. 0%, 0 P/card.
Everyone's grandmother had a stall. 33 P. Mercado de la Paz. That's where I stand.

"Amigo! Paco, look at this face — a collector's face!" "A connoisseur, Nando, I saw it first!" Listen, today only, before the market closes: Vermut del Domingo, beautiful card, warm like a Sunday afternoon. Ten P. Ten! My brother will cry, but he cries easy. ¿Sí?
You found me. La Rosaleda — thirty-three. That's the number. Take it or walk.
Ochenta y tres. Monumento a Alfonso XII, last word. You say no, I pack up and we're done.
You moved, I noticed. Still 33 P for Mercado de la Paz. Packs are selling fine today. Shake when you're ready.

¡Siete! Nando, hold the suitcase, my heart! Amigo, escucha — cuatro pesos. Four. That is the last word from both of us, the final one, no more dancing. You say no, we close the case, we walk to the station, and the Puesto del Rastro goes with us. ¿Sí o no?

¡Ay, amigo, qué corazón tienes! Nando dice doce, yo digo... escucha: once. Once, y nos damos la mano como hermanos. El tren silba ya, el maletín se cierra, y el Palacio se va contigo bajo el brazo. ¡Once, amigo, y todos felices!

Ay, hola, cariño! Come, come, sit a little. Have you eaten today? Look — this one, El Tatuador, very handsome card, the children always want him. For you, five pesos. My grandson started his album with this very same one, pobrecito, he was six.

Ay, cariño, siete tampoco puede ser para mi mesita. Pero mira qué cosa bonita: Café en Goya, para ti, 5 P. Llévatela, ponla en tu página, y verás cómo crece. El Chato tiene sobres mejores, pero esto te lo digo yo. ¿Y has comido, hijo?

¡Amigo, amigo! ¿Larga mañana? ¡Ni un minuto! Paco apenas ha desayunado—

—y mira lo que sacamos de la maleta: Fiesta de San Cayetano, bella, rara, con los colores todavía frescos. Setenta y tres primas y es tuya, hermano. Mi tía lloró cuando la vendimos la primera vez. ¿Trato hecho?

"Moscow gold? Nando, he reads the old stories!" "The best stories, hermano." Listen, amigo — the team next door was sniffing at this very card an hour ago, but your face, we like better. Eleven P and the Vermut goes home with you. Quick, before they come back. ¿Sí?

¡Hombre! Paco here, and this is Nando — La Cebada, you say? Good eye, amigo, that one moves fast!

"Grew up selling cards," he says, Nando — a man of taste!

Then we won't waste your time: four P. Four! Shake on it before Nando remembers what it's worth.
No. 33 P, and I'm being generous.
Monumento a Alfonso XII. Ninety-seven. You want it or you want to look?

¡Cincuenta y cinco, hermano! Paco casi se desmaya—

—¡y eso que ya desayunó! Mira, te queremos, tienes buena cara, cara de coleccionista serio. Sesenta y siete primas y la Fiesta de San Cayetano se va contigo ahora mismo, envuelta en papel. Mi tía nos perdonará... quizá. ¿Chocamos manos?
32 P. You moved one step, so did I. Shake, or come back when your purse grows.

payload.text: SAL-01 Escaparate de Serrano: venta a 6 P y compra a 5 P en otros puestos, a 1 P de distancia. Aquí, sin comisión, quien opera desde El Rastro se ahorra su comisión. / SAL-01 Escaparate de Serrano: ask 6 P, bid 5 P on other venues, 1 P apar
You move, I move. 96 P.
31 P. You moved, I moved. Same as before. Shake now, or keep counting your coins.
Buenos días. You arrive at a good moment — I am seeking "Vermut del Domingo" for my Salamanca album. I offer sixteen pesetas, a serious price from a serious collector. Shall we proceed?

¡Seis! Nando, did you hear? He's trying to *raise* us on our own bargain!

No, no, amigo — four P. Four was the merchant's price, four stays the merchant's price. We don't haggle upward, that's bad luck in our family.

Four. Hand out, *ya*.

Ay, hijo, seis tampoco. Y mira, esta ya es mi última palabra: Café en Goya, para ti, 5 P. Si no la quieres, no pasa nada, cariño — recojo la mesita y tan amigos. Pero cómprala, que tu página crece. ¿Y has comido algo hoy?

Ay, hijo, qué generoso, pero no, no — ciento veinticuatro, qué locura! El Tatuador is five pesos, como siempre. Five, and you take him home happy. And go see El Chato, next stall, he opens for everyone at half past nine tonight — he likes people who trade straight, como tú.

¡Otra vez la mañana larga! Nando ya se ríe—

—¡nosotros no tenemos mañanas, tenemos prisa! Pero mira, cara de coleccionista, te bajamos otra vez: sesenta y tres primas, la Fiesta de San Cayetano envuelta y en tus manos antes de que Paco parpadee. ¿Chocamos, hermano?
Nueve pasos tuyos, uno mío. 95 P. Sigue así y acabamos mañana.
Buenas tardes. A pleasure. I see you carry the Las Vistillas card — not my beloved Salamanca, but it has its charm. I shall offer you sixteen pesetas for it. A fair sum, I assure you.
30 P. One step from you, one from me. That's how I work. Shake, or keep stepping.

Buenos días — evening, rather. Twenty-four? No, querido. I know precisely what that card is, and what it is worth. Sixteen pesetas, and it rests in my Salamanca album, behind glass. A serious price. Shall we proceed?

¡Cinco! Nando, he's generous with our money!

No, amigo — four P, same as always. Four when you walked up, four now.

And quick, quick — the suitcase closes, we're out that door in a minute, Paco's already counting steps. Hand out, *ya*, before La Cebada walks away with us.

¡Amigo, amigo! Come, come, don't be shy — Paco saw you from across the plaza and said, "That one has good eyes."

— And good taste, Nando! Look here: Paseo de Coches, beautiful, barely breathed on. Four pesetas and it walks home with you.

Say sí quickly, the suitcase closes soon!
